english.title: Fail to inspect knife before killing animal in accordance with religious rites and ensure severance by rapid movements
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), when killing a

(A)_[sheep]_
(B)_[goat]_
(C)_[bovine animal]_

in accordance with religious rites without prior stunning, failed to

(D)_[ensure it was killed by the severance of both its carotid arteries and jugular veins by rapid, uninterrupted movements of a hand-held knife]_
(E)_[immediately before killing, inspect the knife to be used to ensure it was undamaged and of sufficient size and sharpness to kill the sheep, goat or bovine animal by the severance of both its carotid arteries and jugular veins by rapid, uninterrupted movements]_
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 30(1)(e) and 33(1) of, and paragraph 5 of Schedule 3 to. the Welfare of Animals at the Time of Killing (England) Regulations 2015.

other.penalty:
Summary: Fine

Time limit for prosecutions
6 monthsNote
Note that for offences committed since 12 March 2015, section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012 removes the limits on certain fines given by the Magistrates' Courts. Offences that were previously punishable by fines of 'prescribed sums' and that were limited to 'not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale' or 'not exceeding the statutory maximum', are now punishable by a fine of any amount.
